item.title: Give the Agent a Desk, Not Your Keys
item.description: You would never give a new hire root on the machine holding your keys. Kagebox is an experiment in giving an autonomous agent a whole machine that is not yours: its own kernel, credentials that stay host side, a latch it cannot reach, and a spend cap. Every layer of it can fail open without saying so, and that turned out to be the lesson.

item.title: Agentic Development Needs Its Methodology Moment
item.description: Waterfall gave us definition. Agile gave us feedback. CI gave us a referee. AI agents are the next leap in who writes software, and the teams winning with them are not the ones with the cleverest prompts. They are the ones who gave their agent a methodology. A field guide from a real project.

item.title: The AI Writes the Screenplay, the Renderer Never Lies
item.description: Generative video is a slot machine: same prompt, different pixels every run. vsim flips the design. The AI writes a validated screenplay document, and a deterministic pure TypeScript renderer turns it into the same MP4, byte for byte, on any machine, forever.

item.title: You Do Not Trust the Output. You Trust the Loop.
item.description: Vibe coding and agentic coding get ranked like a difficulty setting. They are not points on a scale. They are opposites, separated by one thing: whether you trust a single output or a process that earns it.

item.title: The Skills That Compound With AI Aren't Technical
item.description: Here is something worth noticing about AI-assisted building. The people getting the most out of it are not always the strongest coders. Often they are people with a different set of traits entirely.
